extracted.intended_audience: Mathematica / Wolfram Language programmers developing larger systems and packages
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on stylistic elements of Mathematica programming for organizing related routines or large algorithms into packages and for providing associated documentation, error handling, and variable localization. Focused on producing maintainable, efficient, and elegant Mathematica code for larger systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package-based organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Place a series of related routines, or a single large algorithm, into a package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large systems, collect related routines into a package so the code is organized, reusable, and modular. Packaging is the usual approach for grouping code in Mathematica and helps manage complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include ancillary information in packages
rubrics_metrics.description: The package not only collects these routines, but contains ancillary information such as usage messages, error messages, and variable localization constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A package should carry its supporting metadata and mechanisms—documentation hooks, runtime diagnostics, and scoping constructs—so that the code is self-describing and behaves correctly when used in larger contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage messages / documentation for functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide usage messages (documentation) for functions included in the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose clear usage messages so users of the package understand function purpose, arguments, and expected behavior. Treat documentation as an integral part of the code distribution rather than an afterthought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error messages and signalling
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and design error messages in the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide informative error messages to help diagnose misuse or runtime problems. Error messaging is part of the package's interface and contributes to robustness and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable localization / scoping constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use variable localization constructs to manage scope within packages and avoid unwanted interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize variables to prevent name collisions and side effects when packages are loaded into a notebook/session. Scoping is a stylistic and correctness concern in Mathematica system design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for efficient and elegant code
rubrics_metrics.description: Write code that is both efficient and elegant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style includes choices that affect readability and performance; aim for implementations that balance clarity, conciseness, and computational efficiency. Examples and patterns illustrating efficient idioms are part of style guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide programming examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompany routines and packages with programming examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including examples demonstrates intended use, clarifies edge cases, and serves as informal tests and documentation for users of the package.
